## Before/after evals (2026-11-09 PST)

Before: origin/main 872e7f6c3fd (Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6). After: 0ed7010e9e7 (= 6f54ea438de, the upgrade with the reasoning-in-output fix, + spec pins). The later amend b76a747a4f3 adds only the prior-generation window table, which affects explicitly pinned 4.x ids, not 5.5 runs. Bedrock-first via AWS_PROFILE=frontier-bedrock. Prompt evals ran inside a local gate session (workaround for open bug dissocial-unpleasant-adouri; without it every case scores 0.00) at REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES=12, mirroring the eval-live loop. Provider parity: python -m rebar.llm.evals.provider_parity --concurrency 4, 50-item corpus, 3 epochs.

Reading: no spec regressed from PASS to FAIL; code-review-api-compat and spec-alignment moved FAIL to PASS. Every spec failing on 5.5 fails identically on 4.x: three have no solver (bug knightly-salty-orangutan, coverage 0.00 on both), seven plan-review specs fail schema validation on a 'dimension' field on both, and the rest are false-fire/miss gates on both. Parity: both 5.5 slots are invalid=false with zero sampling_parameter/auth_validation errors (the 4.x standard slot had 13+17 step-budget/runaway errors; 5.5 has none). The 5.5 standard slot has 1 gold-regressing flip (ELE-F1, block on direct, advisory on Bedrock; one gold-improving flip NETMECH-F1 the other way), so it does not meet the 0-flip parity bar; the 4.x frontier slot failed the same bar with 1 flip plus a false-accept rise. A single 3-epoch run cannot separate model change from run-to-run noise at n=50.
